rules: The detector/XAI evidence comes before ATT&CK contextualization.
The LLM may select only from allowed candidates supplied for the observed class.
The LLM must not invent a technique ID, attack class, feature, or evidence.
Candidate/conditional techniques must retain their qualification text.
Flow-level XAI is supporting evidence, not proof of host/browser execution or persistence.

mappings.important_rule: Use only the candidates below. Do not create a new ATT&CK ID. A conditional/candidate mapping requires the listed qualification evidence.

allowed_mitre_candidates.reason: CIC-IoT-2023 defines Backdoor Malware as installing malware that creates a hidden entry point for later unauthorized access. Because this is a web-based attack and the dataset uses DVWA/Remot3d, T1505.003 is a reasonable contextual candidate when the observed backdoor is implemented as a web shell or web-accessible server-side script.
allowed_mitre_candidates.qualification: Do not mark T1505.003 as confirmed from flow features alone. Confirm with web-root/file-creation/process evidence or a documented web-shell implementation.

allowed_mitre_candidates.reason: The dataset's Browser Hijacking attack modifies browser settings such as the home page, search engine, or bookmarks and redirects the user. T1185 covers browser/session hijacking, but its ATT&CK definition is more specific to session takeover, cookies, certificates, or browser pivoting.
allowed_mitre_candidates.qualification: Keep this as a candidate only. Do not report T1185 as confirmed unless host/browser telemetry demonstrates session hijacking behavior.

allowed_mitre_candidates.reason: T1189 includes malicious script injection into web pages, but the dataset's Browser Hijacking label does not by itself prove a drive-by compromise.
allowed_mitre_candidates.qualification: Use only when browser/network evidence shows compromise through a user's visit to attacker-controlled or compromised web content.

allowed_mitre_candidates.reason: CIC-IoT-2023 describes Command Injection as targeting a web application by injecting commands into an input field. MITRE T1190 explicitly covers exploitation of Internet-facing web applications/services.
allowed_mitre_candidates.qualification: The mapping identifies the exploitation context. Flow-only data does not prove which command interpreter was executed after exploitation.

allowed_mitre_candidates.reason: The dataset states that successful Command Injection can result in arbitrary command execution. T1059 covers adversary abuse of command/script interpreters.
allowed_mitre_candidates.qualification: Only promote to a reported technique when endpoint/process telemetry or application logs show the interpreter used. Do not guess a sub-technique such as PowerShell, Windows Command Shell, Unix Shell, or JavaScript.

allowed_mitre_candidates.technique_name: Network Denial of Service: Direct Network Flood
allowed_mitre_candidates.reason: CIC-IoT-2023 documents GREETH as a Mirai flood attack using packet encapsulation based on the Ethernet header. MITRE T1498.001 covers direct high-volume network floods, including attacks using many protocols.
allowed_mitre_candidates.qualification: The ZeroShield flow evidence supports anomaly detection of the flood behavior; ATT&CK attribution is contextual, not a replacement for the detector.

allowed_mitre_candidates.technique_name: Network Denial of Service: Direct Network Flood
allowed_mitre_candidates.reason: CIC-IoT-2023 documents GREIP as a Mirai flood in which GRE packets carry encapsulated traffic. MITRE T1498.001 covers direct high-volume network flooding against a target.
allowed_mitre_candidates.qualification: The ATT&CK mapping is made from the known attack label/behavior plus network-flow evidence; it is not inferred from one feature alone.

allowed_mitre_candidates.technique_name: Network Denial of Service: Direct Network Flood
allowed_mitre_candidates.reason: CIC-IoT-2023 documents UDPPlain as a Mirai attack that floods the target with UDP packets. MITRE T1498.001 explicitly includes UDP as a common protocol for direct flood attacks.
allowed_mitre_candidates.qualification: Treat this as ATT&CK context for a known dataset attack class, not as an independent classification result from Deep SVDD.

allowed_mitre_candidates.reason: CIC-IoT-2023 defines SQL Injection as malicious SQL code injected into web-application input. MITRE T1190 explicitly discusses exploiting websites and databases and includes SQL injection in its procedure examples.
allowed_mitre_candidates.qualification: Flow-level XAI explains the anomalous network behavior; it does not prove the exact SQL payload or post-exploitation effect.

allowed_mitre_candidates.reason: CIC-IoT-2023 describes Uploading Attack as exploiting a web application's file-upload functionality to upload malicious files and potentially execute arbitrary code. That is consistent with exploitation of a web-facing application.
allowed_mitre_candidates.qualification: Report T1190 as the exploitation context. Exact application vulnerability and post-upload execution require application/host evidence.

allowed_mitre_candidates.reason: The dataset describes malicious-file upload into the target environment. MITRE T1105 covers transfer of tools or files from an external system into a compromised environment.
allowed_mitre_candidates.qualification: Keep this as secondary context unless the observed workflow clearly shows a malicious file being transferred into an already-compromised environment.

allowed_mitre_candidates.reason: CIC-IoT-2023 defines XSS as injecting malicious script into a web page for execution by a browser. MITRE T1189 explicitly lists cross-site scripting as a way malicious scripts or iFrames may be inserted into a compromised website.
allowed_mitre_candidates.qualification: Because the ZeroShield inputs are flow-level, do not claim browser execution unless browser/client telemetry confirms the follow-on behavior.
